whatItIs.text: Pure starch from the corn kernel's endosperm — the quiet thickener behind glossy sauces, custards, and crisp-fried anything; cornflour, in British English.

historyNote.text: Until 1851 corn starch was mostly a laundry product; the culinary kind was patented in 1854 by John Polson of Brown & Polson in Paisley, Scotland — muslin makers who became the UK's largest starch producers.

howToChoose.text: Any plain box works; skip pre-mixed 'gravy thickeners' with additives, and buy the smallest box if you thicken rarely — it keeps for ages either way.

storage.text: Keep in an airtight container in a dry cupboard.

useItUp.text: Beyond sauces, cornstarch crispst — toss chicken or tofu in it before frying, or whisk a slurry into soup when it needs body; it never flours the flavour.

substitutions.note: glossier, freeze-thaw stable; add at the end
works but clouds sauces and needs longer cooking
